function_v0.doc:
Buy `tres_amount` (share base units) at the current price. Returns the
payment cost in stroops. The buyer authorizes both this call and the
payment transfer out of their account.

The payment stays in this contract rather than going straight to the
treasury: that balance is what the buyback draws on.
function_v0.name: buy

function_v0.doc:
Sell `tres_amount` (share base units) back to the contract. Returns the
payment received, net of the fee. The seller authorizes both this call
and the share transfer out of their account.

Shares return to inventory and become sellable again. The fee goes to
the treasury; the rest goes to the seller.
function_v0.name: sell

function_v0.doc: Payment cost (stroops) to buy `tres_amount` share base units.
function_v0.name: quote

function_v0.doc: Payment received (stroops) for selling `tres_amount` back, fee deducted.\nThis is the authoritative number to show a seller.

function_v0.doc: Admin: withdraw sale proceeds. Whatever is left behind is what remains\navailable for buybacks, so this is the lever that decides how much\nliquidity the window offers.
function_v0.name: withdraw_pay

function_v0.doc:
Runs once at deploy.

* `price` \xe2\x80\x94 payment-asset stroops per one whole share.
* `buyback_price` \xe2\x80\x94 same unit; `0` closes the buyback window.
* `fee_bps` \xe2\x80\x94 fee taken on buybacks only, in basis points (500 = 5%).
* `auto_allow` \xe2\x80\x94 whether to allowlist buyers on the token before
delivering shares. Requires this contract to hold the token's `admin`
role. Set it to `false` for a plain SAC, which has no allowlist.
